organizations.name: Run For Something
organizations.for: young progressives (Millennials and Gen Z) thinking about a first or second run for local or state office
organizations.offers: a call with staff and other would-be candidates, then online trainings, referrals, mentors, and a national network

organizations.name: Working Families Party: Working Class Wins
organizations.for: working people (nurses, drivers, organizers) who want to run as a Working Families Democrat or independent; the party has its own ballot line in New York
organizations.offers: a sign-up to learn the basics of running and how to seek the party's backing, plus training and a network

organizations.name: Emerge
organizations.for: Democratic women thinking about running for office
organizations.offers: a free 90-minute intro session, and state programs such as Emerge Virginia's six-month, 70-hour candidate course

organizations.name: The Collective PAC
organizations.for: progressive Black candidates running at the local, state, or federal level
organizations.offers: an endorsement, with training, technical help, and fundraising support; applications for 2027 races open Dec. 1, 2026

organizations.name: NEA See Educators Run
organizations.for: teachers and school staff in the National Education Association who are running or thinking about it
organizations.offers: a three-day union training on vote goals, your pitch, and building a slate of candidates

organizations.name: Virginia Education Association: Running for Office
organizations.for: VEA members in Virginia's public schools who are thinking about running for state or local office
organizations.offers: a workshop, on request, on whether you're ready, Virginia election and campaign-finance law, organizing, and fundraising

organizations.name: NYSUT Pipeline Project
organizations.for: members of New York State United Teachers who want to run, from school board to the Legislature
organizations.offers: training and help from the union's regional political organizers for members who run

organizations.name: Vote Run Lead
organizations.for: women and gender-expansive people who want to run, of any party
organizations.offers: an online library of worksheets, videos, and guides for planning and running a campaign

organizations.name: New American Leaders
organizations.for: immigrants, refugees, and children of immigrants thinking about public office
organizations.offers: a weekend training on your stump speech, fundraising, and messaging; $150, with some scholarships

organizations.name: LGBTQ+ Victory Institute
organizations.for: LGBTQ+ people thinking about running, and the people who staff their campaigns
organizations.offers: a free one-day Candidate & Campaign 101 and multi-day campaign bootcamps (with a fee)

organizations.name: Women Winning: run for office
organizations.for: pro-choice women in Minnesota who are running for any office or thinking about it; the group calls itself nonpartisan but backs only pro-choice candidates
organizations.offers: free trainings for candidates and campaign staff, one-on-one coaching on campaign plans and budgets, and a competitive endorsement that can bring money, volunteers, and promotion

organizations.name: Minnesota AFL-CIO: Run for Office
organizations.for: union members in Minnesota who are running, thinking about running, or want to work on campaigns
organizations.offers: a two-day training each year on campaign plans, messaging, public speaking, volunteers, fundraising, and campaign finance rules; the 2026 session was in May, and if you fill out the page's form, staff will follow up about the 2027 one

organizations.name: Minnesota School Boards Association: running for school board
organizations.for: anyone in Minnesota thinking about running for their local school board
organizations.offers: a short video on running, a guide to what board members do, a candidate FAQ and key dates for school board elections, and links to the state's election guides and campaign finance manual

organizations.name: New Jersey Working Families Party
organizations.for: progressive candidates in New Jersey, from county commissioner to Congress, who want the party's backing
organizations.offers: a link to apply for the party's endorsement, plus its endorsed candidates and voter guides; in 2026 it backed county commissioner candidates, including four in Hudson County, and congressional candidates in the 10th, 11th, and 12th districts

organizations.name: New Jersey School Boards Association: school board candidate kit
organizations.for: anyone in New Jersey thinking about running for their local school board
organizations.offers: sample nominating petitions (you need 25 signatures, filed with your county clerk), a school election FAQ and calendar, county clerk contacts, a recorded webinar on campaign finance rules, and what new board members must do; petitions for the Nov. 3, 2026 school board races were due July 27, 2026

organizations.name: Emerge Georgia: signature program
organizations.for: Democratic women and nonbinary people in Georgia who plan to run for office and already have a record of community work
organizations.offers: a six-month, 70-hour candidate training with campaign experts and elected officials; tuition is $750, which Emerge encourages you to raise with its grassroots fundraising training instead of paying; on Nov. 14, 2026 the page still showed the deadline for the Class of 2026 (Nov. 26, 2025), so ask about the next class

organizations.name: Georgia Working Families Party
organizations.for: progressive and working-class candidates in Georgia, from city council to Congress, who want the party's backing
organizations.offers: a link to apply for the party's endorsement, plus its endorsed candidates and news; the party says it won 16 Georgia primaries in 2026, and its Southern Made campaign, launched July 2026, aims to recruit and train 1,000 working-class candidates across the South by 2030

organizations.name: Asian Americans Advancing Justice-Atlanta: nonpartisan candidate training
organizations.for: anyone thinking of running for local, state, or federal office in Georgia, from school board and city council to Congress; the group works especially to bring Asian American and immigrant Georgians into office
organizations.offers: a two-day training, held since 2013, on campaign plans, messaging, fundraising and legal compliance, volunteers, media, and election law, with an application; on Nov. 14, 2026 the page still showed the Sept. 5 and 6, 2025 class in Norcross as closed, so ask elections@advancingjustice-atlanta.org about the next one

organizations.name: Georgia Association of Educators: board candidate support
organizations.for: Georgia public school employees in the teachers' union (the state affiliate of the NEA) who are thinking about running for school board or other office
organizations.offers: a short page making the case for educators in office, which sends you to the NEA's See Educators Run candidate training; it lists no Georgia-only training or dates

how_to_run.name: Virginia Department of Elections: becoming a candidate
how_to_run.offers: the step-by-step list for getting on a Virginia ballot: who qualifies, the forms, voter petitions, fees, and deadlines, with a guide for each office

how_to_run.name: New York State Board of Elections: running for office
how_to_run.offers: who can hold each office, the petition rules for party and independent candidates, and the filing calendar

how_to_run.name: NYC Board of Elections: for candidates
how_to_run.offers: petition forms and guidelines, the filing calendar, campaign finance reports, and where to file in each borough

how_to_run.name: NYC Campaign Finance Board: matching funds
how_to_run.offers: public money for city races: each NYC resident's donation is matched 8 to 1 on up to $250 ($175 for City Council), so small donations go much further

how_to_run.name: Virginia Beach Voter Registration & Elections: candidacy and campaign finance
how_to_run.offers: where to get candidate filing forms, a tool to check which election district you live in, when each local office is next on the ballot, and the campaign finance reporting rules

how_to_run.name: Chesapeake Voter Registrar: becoming a candidate
how_to_run.offers: the basic qualifications to run, with links to the state's candidate bulletin for each office, the filing forms, campaign finance reporting, and the city's political sign rules

how_to_run.name: Suffolk General Registrar: candidate resources and requirements
how_to_run.offers: who can run for city council and school board, which borough seats are on the ballot, how many petition signatures each office needs, and the city's rules for campaign finance and political signs

how_to_run.name: Gloucester Elections & Voter Registration: become a candidate
how_to_run.offers: when you can file to run, the campaign committee, bank account, and finance-report rules you'll have to follow, and a link to the state's full candidate guide

how_to_run.name: Minnesota Secretary of State: become a candidate
how_to_run.offers: how to get on a Minnesota ballot: you file an affidavit of candidacy and pay a filing fee (or turn in a petition) during the filing period, with a guide for each office, from the Legislature to county board, city council, school board, and township

how_to_run.name: Minneapolis Elections & Voter Services: filing for office
how_to_run.offers: the steps to get on a Minneapolis ballot: you file in person at 980 E. Hennepin Ave. during the filing period and pay $20 to $500 depending on the office, or turn in a petition of up to 500 signatures; mayor, council, park board, and Board of Estimate and Taxation races use ranked-choice voting (rank up to three), and the next filing period is in 2028, for School Board

how_to_run.name: Ramsey County Elections: ranked voting in Saint Paul
how_to_run.offers: how Saint Paul's city races are won: voters rank the candidates, and if no one gets a majority of first choices, the votes are reallocated to pick a winner; the school board race isn't ranked. The city pays Ramsey County to run its elections, so candidates file in person at the county elections office, 90 W. Plato Blvd.

how_to_run.name: Ramsey County Elections: candidate filing
how_to_run.offers: who can run (an eligible voter who will be 21 by the time they take office and has lived in the district for 30 days before the election), the affidavit of candidacy for each kind of office, and the campaign finance rules; questions go to 651-266-2171

how_to_run.name: St. Louis County Elections: candidate filing
how_to_run.offers: links for anyone running for county, city, town, or school board office in St. Louis County: who to file with and when, the affidavit forms, the county's filing notice, and campaign finance reports; questions go to elections@stlouiscountymn.gov or 218-726-2385

how_to_run.name: New Jersey Division of Elections: candidate information
how_to_run.offers: the state's page for candidates for Congress, Governor, and the Legislature, who file their petitions with the Division of Elections in Trenton; the 2026 filing period is over, and the page says petitions and instructions for 2027, when all 120 legislative seats are on the ballot, will be posted in 2027; it also links to the rules for petition challenges and campaign finance

how_to_run.name: New Jersey Division of Elections: election timelines
how_to_run.offers: a date-by-date calendar for each kind of New Jersey election, with every petition filing deadline: the June party primary, the November general election, May nonpartisan city elections (the kind Newark holds), school board, and fire district elections; the 2027 calendars weren't posted as of Nov. 14, 2026

how_to_run.name: Union County Clerk: candidate petitions
how_to_run.offers: who you file with for each kind of race: county offices and November school board seats file with the County Clerk's Election Division (908-527-4996, 2 Broad St., Elizabeth), and city and town races file with your municipal clerk, so Elizabeth candidates file with the Elizabeth City Clerk; party primary petitions are due by 4 p.m. on the 71st day before the primary, independents file by 4 p.m. on primary day, and Hillside is the county's only town with nonpartisan elections

how_to_run.name: Camden County: information for candidates
how_to_run.offers: where each kind of candidate files: Sheriff, County Clerk, Surrogate, County Commissioner, and school board petitions go to the County Clerk's Election Division at 100 University Ct., Blackwood; party primary and May nonpartisan petitions for mayor and council go to your municipal clerk; independents for November file with the County Clerk by primary day; primary petitions are due by 4 p.m. on the 71st day before the June primary, signatures must be in ink and collected in person, and the petition forms are on the page

how_to_run.name: Atlantic County Clerk: candidate information
how_to_run.offers: nominating petitions for county, municipal (including Atlantic City mayor and council), county committee, independent, school board, and fire commissioner candidates, with how many signatures each office needs for 2026 and 2027 and the current candidate lists

how_to_run.name: Fulton County Registration and Elections: candidate information
how_to_run.offers: who you qualify with for each race: county offices go through the department's qualifying officers (404-612-7020, 5600 Campbellton Fairburn Road, Union City), except that party candidates for county office qualify with the county Democratic or Republican Party, and city candidates, including Atlanta's, qualify with their city clerk; the linked 2026 packet shows qualifying ran March 2 to 6, 2026, with fees of $1,950 for a district commission seat, $3,600 for commission chair, and $747 for school board, paid to whoever you qualify with

how_to_run.name: DeKalb County Voter Registration and Elections: candidate information
how_to_run.offers: the 2026 county qualifying guide and fee list (qualifying ran March 2 to 6, 2026; fees were $2,101.28 for county commissioner and $750 for school board), with sign, campaign-activity, and poll-watcher rules; nonpartisan and independent candidates qualify with the elections office at 4380 Memorial Drive, Decatur (404-298-4020), party candidates with the county Democratic or Republican Party, and city candidates file with their city clerk; county candidates file campaign reports with the elections board

how_to_run.name: Cobb County Elections: qualifying for office
how_to_run.offers: the 2026 county qualifying notice and the final lists of qualified candidates; qualifying ran March 2 to 6, 2026: nonpartisan candidates (State Court judges) qualified with the elections board at 995 Roswell St. NE, Marietta, and partisan candidates with the county Democratic Party (678-223-3705) or Republican Party (770-272-0458), with fees of $1,728.82 for a district commission seat and $570 for school board; questions go to 770-528-2581

how_to_run.name: Marietta City Clerk: election information
how_to_run.offers: how to run for mayor or City Council: you file your notice of candidacy with the City Clerk at City Hall, 205 Lawrence St., 4th floor, during a three-day qualifying period (for the Nov. 4, 2025 election it was Aug. 18 to 20, 2025); you must be 21 and a qualified voter, mayoral candidates must have lived in Marietta for a year and council candidates in their ward for a year, terms are four years, and a runoff follows if no one wins a majority; the page hadn't posted the next election's dates as of Nov. 14, 2026

how_to_run.name: Gwinnett County Elections: running for office
how_to_run.offers: who you qualify with and what it costs: party candidates for county office qualify with the county Democratic or Republican Party (contact emails on the page), nonpartisan candidates at the elections office at 455 Grayson Highway, Suite 200, Lawrenceville, and independents file nomination petitions (in 2026, June 22 to July 14 at noon); 2026 fees were $1,350 for a district commission seat and $730.25 for school board, paid to whoever you qualify with; with the 2026 qualified candidate list

how_to_run.name: Lawrenceville City Clerk: qualifying for candidacy
how_to_run.offers: what it takes to run for mayor or City Council, in English and Spanish: you must have lived in Lawrenceville for a year by Election Day and be a registered voter, and you pay a $378 qualifying fee for council or $600 for mayor (3 percent of the pay) to the City Clerk, who runs city elections; terms are four years and staggered, with a 12-year limit; the next general election is Nov. 2, 2027, and qualifying packets are available at City Hall, 70 S. Clayton St., in election years (678-407-6389)

how_to_run.name: Chatham County Board of Elections: 2026 qualifying notice
how_to_run.offers: where and when candidates qualified for 2026 county races: nonpartisan candidates (school board, Recorder's Court judge) at the Board of Elections, 1117 Eisenhower Drive, Suite F, Savannah (912-201-4375), and party candidates with the Democratic Party of Chatham County (912-272-7972) or the Chatham County Republican Party (912-356-3800), March 2 to 6, 2026; fees were $750 for a school board district seat and $1,050 for school board president; a PDF, posted on the board's home page each election year

how_to_run.name: Savannah Clerk of Council: elections
how_to_run.offers: the city's page for candidates for mayor and the eight aldermen, all elected without party labels; the Clerk of Council qualifies candidates at City Hall, 2 E. Bay St. (912-651-6441), and the next city election is Nov. 2, 2027, when all nine seats are up; the linked 2023 packet shows a five-day qualifying week in late August and fees of 3 percent of salary ($1,710 for mayor, $750 for alderman), and candidates must be 18, with six months' residence in their district or a year in the city for mayor and at-large posts

how_to_run.name: Muscogee County Elections and Registration: candidate information
how_to_run.offers: the elections office's home page, whose Elected Officials & Candidate menu has the qualifying fees, the list of qualified candidates, campaign disclosure forms, and every local candidate's filed reports; mayor, council, and school board races in Columbus are nonpartisan, and candidates qualified with this office (3111 Citizens Way, 2nd floor, 706-653-4392) March 2 to 6, 2026, paying $1,950 for mayor and $360 for council or school board

how_to_run.name: Athens-Clarke County Elections: qualified candidates, 2026
how_to_run.offers: who qualified with the county elections office for the May 19, 2026 local races, day by day from March 2 to 6, 2026: mayor, the odd-numbered commission and school board districts (the only ones up in 2026), and solicitor general, with links to candidates' campaign filings; mayor and commission races are nonpartisan, and the elections office at 155 E. Washington St. (706-613-3150) has qualifying details for the next cycle

how_to_run.name: Georgia.gov: run for public office
how_to_run.offers: the state's step-by-step guide: the four ways onto a Georgia ballot (a party primary, a political body's petition or convention, an independent petition, or write-in), the partisan, nonpartisan, and county offices you can run for, and how qualifying works: state candidates qualify during set weeks, local candidates with their county or city elections office, everyone pays a fee or files a pauper's affidavit and petition, and you bring a photo ID and your candidacy form; its links for forms and fees go to the Secretary of State's site

boards.name: Secretary of the Commonwealth: state boards and commissions
boards.offers: how to apply online for the roughly 900 seats the governor fills each year on state boards; most boards meet about four times a year

boards.name: Brooklyn Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: apply online or on paper to your Brooklyn community board; open to New Yorkers 16 and up, unpaid, about 6 to 8 hours a month; 2027 applications due Feb. 8, 2027

boards.name: Bronx Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: how Bronx community boards work and who gets appointed; unpaid seats, with applications reopening at the end of each year

boards.name: Manhattan Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: what Manhattan community board members do and how to apply; two-year unpaid terms, with a monthly board meeting and at least two committees

boards.name: Queens Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: how to join a Queens community board if you're 16 or older; unpaid two-year terms, with the next application period opening in early January 2027

boards.name: Staten Island Borough President: community board application
boards.offers: apply online or by mail to a Staten Island community board if you live, work, or have a stake in the district; 16- and 17-year-olds can apply

boards.name: Mayor's Office of Appointments: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the list of more than 200 city boards and commissions the mayor appoints, with a form to send your resume and say you want to serve

boards.name: City of Norfolk: apply for a board or commission
boards.offers: the current vacancy list and the online application for more than 50 city boards and commissions; City Council reviews applications every quarter and keeps them on file for a year

boards.name: City of Virginia Beach: Talent Bank application for boards and commissions
boards.offers: the application City Council draws from to fill seats on about 60 boards, commissions, and committees; open to Virginia Beach residents who are registered voters, and kept on file for five years

boards.name: City of Chesapeake: applicants needed for boards and commissions
boards.offers: the current list of open seats, application deadlines and the online application, which goes to the City Clerk

boards.name: City of Portsmouth: boards and commissions
boards.offers: what each city board and commission does, a link to the current vacancy list, and an application you can fill out online or print

boards.name: City of Suffolk: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the city's boards, commissions, and council committees; the page has no application, so ask the City Clerk's office, which handles appointments, at 757-514-4018 or council@suffolkva.us

boards.name: City of Newport News: boards, commissions and committees
boards.offers: how appointments to nearly 45 city boards work, with a link to the online Board Bank application; you must live in Newport News and pass a background check, and City Council appoints every quarter

boards.name: City of Williamsburg: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the online application for city residents to serve on city and regional boards; applications are taken any time and City Council reviews them when a seat opens

boards.name: City of Poquoson: boards and commissions
boards.offers: a printable Board Bank application for U.S. citizens registered to vote in Poquoson, covering 14 boards from the Planning Commission to the Wetlands Board; you turn it in, or a resume and cover letter, at the City Manager's Office

boards.name: York County: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the online Board Bank application, the list of current vacancies, and a guide to each board's requirements and meeting times; about 200 residents serve, appointed by the Board of Supervisors, and applications stay on file for a year

boards.name: Isle of Wight County: board and committee application
boards.offers: an online questionnaire for anyone who wants to serve on a county board, committee, or commission; questions go to County Administration at 757-365-6204

boards.name: Gloucester County: boards and commissions
boards.offers: a link to current vacancies and the application for the county's committees, councils, boards, and commissions, where more than 150 residents volunteer; questions go to County Administration at 804-693-4042

boards.name: Hampton Roads Planning District Commission: Community Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a printable application to join the up-to-30-member public committee that advises the region's planning and transportation boards; open to residents of the 17 member cities and counties, it meets six times a year, for three-year terms

boards.name: Hampton Roads Transit: Transit Riders Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a volunteer committee of up to 14 riders, with at least one from each city HRT serves, that tells HRT how to fix service problems; it meets every other month, and you ask HRT Customer Relations at 757-222-6000 about joining

boards.name: Hampton Roads Transit: Student Transit Riders Commission
boards.offers: an online application for high school students (grades 9 to 12) in the six cities HRT serves; a one-year term with a meeting every month

boards.name: NYC Civic Engagement Commission: Language Assistance Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a volunteer committee that advises the city's program of poll-site interpreters for voters with limited English; applications are taken on a rolling basis, members meet at least every three months, and speaking a second language helps but isn't required

boards.name: James City County: boards, commissions and other agencies
boards.offers: the county’s boards and commissions, with how to apply to serve on one

boards.name: Minnesota Secretary of State: open appointments to state boards
boards.offers: the list of open seats on state boards, councils, and task forces, each with an Apply button; on Nov. 13, 2026 it showed more than 1,000 open seats, filled by the governor, state agencies, and other appointing authorities

boards.name: Metropolitan Council: current advisory committee vacancies
boards.offers: the regional government's open advisory committee seats and its online application; in mid-November 2026 it listed four community seats on the Transportation Advisory Board for two-year terms starting January 2027 (the priority deadline was Nov. 5) and an Equity Advisory Committee seat for District H; TAB members are unpaid, with transit fare, parking, and mileage covered, and meet monthly in downtown St. Paul

boards.name: City of Minneapolis: boards and commissions openings
boards.offers: what's open and how to apply online; the city recruits March 1 to 31 and Aug. 1 to 31, and through Nov. 30, 2026 it's taking applications for the Capital Long-Range Improvement Committee and the Local Board of Appeal and Equalization; you must live in Minneapolis, be 18 or older, and not work for the city, and the Mayor and City Council approve appointments

boards.name: City of Saint Paul: committees, boards, and commissions
boards.offers: the city's more than 30 boards and commissions, grouped by topic, and the online application; applications are taken any time and stay in the pool for the next opening, the Mayor recommends and the City Council approves, and the city suggests asking your council member to back you

boards.name: Ramsey County: advisory boards and committees
boards.offers: current openings (in November 2026, 911 Community Voices and four Charter Commission seats) and the online application; you must live in Ramsey County and be 18 or older or have a parent's consent, and you interview for 10 minutes with three county commissioners; paper applications at 651-266-9200

boards.name: City of Duluth: boards and commissions
boards.offers: about 30 city boards and commissions, from the Planning Commission to the Indigenous Commission, with an Apply button and a list of vacancies; applications are taken any time and kept for a year, the Mayor appoints and the City Council confirms, and most boards meet once or twice a month for an hour or two

boards.name: St. Louis County: application for a citizen advisory committee
boards.offers: the online form to apply for a county advisory committee, commission, or board (you name the one you want); the County Board appoints, and a paper application is available from the Clerk of the County Board at 218-726-2385

boards.name: Governor's Appointments Office: boards, commissions, and authorities
boards.offers: an A-to-Z directory of the state boards, commissions, and authorities the Governor appoints to, with details on each; to apply, you email a current resume naming the board you want to appointments@nj.gov, and the Governor's Appointments Office, (609) 777-0251, has the latest on openings

boards.name: Union County Commissioners: public advisory boards
boards.offers: how to get on a county advisory board: you send a standard application (and a resume when a seat needs a license or skill) to the Clerk of the Board, one for each board you want, and for a term that's ending, at least a month before it ends; the Commissioners' Policy Committee reviews applications, the full board appoints, and applications stay on file for six months; the application form wasn't showing on the county's site on Nov. 14, 2026, so ask the Clerk of the Board at 908-527-4140

boards.name: Camden County: boards, committees and commissions
boards.offers: the county's boards and commissions, from the Environmental Commission and Library Commission to the Cultural Awareness Commission, with what each does and who can serve; the page has no application, so ask the Clerk of the Board of Commissioners at (856) 225-2130

boards.name: City of Camden: become a citizen leader
boards.offers: the Citizen Leadership Form, online or printable in English or Spanish, for city boards, committees, and commissions; you must live in Camden, seats are unpaid, members are expected at regular meetings and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor and City Council, and paper forms go to the Municipal Clerk, City Hall Room 105, or Clerk@camdennj.gov

boards.name: City of Atlantic City: Environmental Commission
boards.offers: the city's call, posted Sept. 8, 2025, for residents to join its new Environmental Commission, which advises city leaders on parks, trees, flooding, litter, food security, and climate; unpaid, monthly meetings, three-year terms (two for alternates), with an online interest form; the page doesn't say whether seats are still open

boards.name: Cobb County Clerk: boards and authorities
boards.offers: about 50 county boards, commissions, and authorities, from the Planning Commission and Library Board to the Transit System Advisory Board and the Opioid Abatement Advisory Council, each with who sits on it, what it does, and how long terms run; commissioners make the appointments, some seats need set qualifications, and there's no application on the page, so ask your district commissioner or the County Clerk's Office at (770) 528-3307

boards.name: City of Marietta: boards and committees
boards.offers: the application for a city board or commission, which goes to the City Clerk's Office, and links to each board, from the Planning Commission and Board of Zoning Appeals to the Power & Water board, Civil Service Board, and Historic Preservation Commission; applications are kept for a year and reviewed when a seat opens on the board you picked

boards.name: Gwinnett County Clerk: apply to serve on a board
boards.offers: the online application to serve on a county board, authority, or committee, sent to your district commissioner or to the chairwoman for an at-large seat, with a link to the list of boards and what each does; each commissioner has dozens of appointments to make

boards.name: City of Lawrenceville: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the city's boards, from the Planning Commission, Board of Appeals, and Housing Authority to the Arts Commission, Financial Review Citizen Committee, and ReCAST Advisory Board for youth programs, with what each does; the page has no application form, so ask the City Clerk, who handles appointments, at 678-407-6389

boards.name: Chatham County Commission: board and authority application process
boards.offers: how to ask for a seat on a county board or authority: email or mail a letter naming the board you want, with your resume, to the commission chairman (chairman@chathamcounty.org) and the Clerk of Commission (jbocook@chathamcounty.org, P.O. Box 8161, Savannah, GA 31412); appointments are made all year, the commission discusses requests in closed session and votes at its next meeting, and the page links a 2022 packet describing the boards

boards.name: Columbus Clerk of Council: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the Clerk of Council keeps the records of Columbus's boards, authorities, committees, and commissions and who sits on them, and the page's Apply Now button opens the city's online board application

boards.name: Athens-Clarke County Clerk of Commission: boards, authorities, and commissions
boards.offers: the list of about 35 unpaid volunteer boards, from the Planning Commission and Land Bank Authority to the Human Relations Commission and Public Safety Civilian Oversight Board, with a handbook on what members do; the Mayor and Commission fill most seats several times a year, often after interviews, and announce openings on the county site, in media releases, and on social media; as of Nov. 14, 2026 the page said no seats were taking applications (questions: 706-613-3031)

boards.name: Georgia Governor's Office: apply for a board, authority, or commission
boards.offers: the online application for the hundreds of state board seats the governor fills: you upload your resume as a PDF named with your first and last name and the governor's board application form, name the board you want, and acknowledge that your application is public; the governor's office changes hands on Jan. 11, 2027, and the form still carries a leftover line about U.S. Senate qualifications from 2019

boards.name: Fulton County Clerk to the Commission: boards and authorities
boards.offers: a fact sheet for each of the more than 60 boards, authorities, and commissions the county appoints to, from the Board of Health and Library Board to the Citizens Commission on the Environment and the Reparations Task Force, with what each does, who appoints (some seats are named by one district commissioner, others by the full board), terms, any pay, meeting times, and current members; there's no application form, so ask your district commissioner or the Clerk to the Commission at 404-612-8200

poll_work.name: Virginia Department of Elections: officers of election
poll_work.offers: how to sign up to work the polls anywhere in Virginia, with training before Election Day; pay depends on your role and your city or county, and the state says not every officer is paid

poll_work.name: New York State Board of Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: paid for training and for each day you work; you're assigned in your own county, and the sign-up form goes to your county board of elections

poll_work.name: NYC Board of Elections: poll worker positions
poll_work.offers: paid poll work as an inspector, interpreter, or 17-year-old poll worker; up to $2,750 for up to 10 days of work; apply online or on paper

poll_work.name: Norfolk Office of Elections: officer of election
poll_work.offers: the interest form for working Norfolk's polls; paid, with a $200 base rate that includes training and more for pollbook officers and chiefs; you stay the whole day, and polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.

poll_work.name: Virginia Beach Voter Registration & Elections: poll worker information
poll_work.offers: the online application to be an election official; $240 for Election Day plus $25 for a three-hour training; you must be 18 or older and a Virginia voter, and stay from 5 a.m. until the polls close and results are in

poll_work.name: Chesapeake Voter Registrar: working the polls
poll_work.offers: an interest form to work at a precinct near your home; $240 for Election Day and $25 for a training class, working from 5 a.m. until about 8 p.m.

poll_work.name: Portsmouth Voter Registration & Elections: becoming an election officer
poll_work.offers: the city's page for working the polls, with training videos; the city asks people who want to serve as an officer of election to contact the Registrar's office

poll_work.name: Suffolk Registrar: officer of election information
poll_work.offers: the online application to work the polls if you're a registered Virginia voter; $250 to $350 for Election Day depending on your role, plus $35 for training, from about 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.

poll_work.name: Newport News Voter Registrar: become an election official
poll_work.offers: the sign-up link for registered Virginia voters to work the polls from 5 a.m. until the count is done; $200 for an officer of election, up to $275 plus $20 for training for a chief officer

poll_work.name: Williamsburg Voter Registrar: working at the polls
poll_work.offers: how to become one of the 40-plus election officers the city needs for a general election, with full-day and half-day shifts; registered voters are paid $150, which covers a two-hour training class and Election Day

poll_work.name: Poquoson Voter Registration & Elections
poll_work.offers: the registrar's page, which links at the top to the state's sign-up form for election officials; it doesn't list pay or training, so call the office at 757-868-3070

poll_work.name: York County Voter Registration: election official information
poll_work.offers: a link to the state's sign-up form for working York County's polls; the page doesn't list pay or training

poll_work.name: Isle of Wight Voter Registration: officer of election information
poll_work.offers: the forms to apply as an officer of election in Isle of Wight County and a short Poll Working 101 video; the page doesn't list pay

poll_work.name: Gloucester Elections & Voter Registration: become an election officer
poll_work.offers: how to apply: pick up the forms at the Elections & Voter Registration office, and the Electoral Board will reply before the next election with training details if you're needed; the page doesn't list pay

poll_work.name: City of Hampton Voter Registrar: becoming an election official
poll_work.offers: how to become an officer of election (poll worker) in Hampton, from the city registrar

poll_work.name: James City County Voter Registration: becoming an election officer
poll_work.offers: how to sign up to work the polls as an officer of election in James City County

poll_work.name: Minneapolis Elections & Voter Services: apply to work on Election Day
poll_work.offers: the online application for the nearly 2,000 election judges the city needs; $17.15 an hour, including a paid training, for a 16-hour day (some half days), and you choose which elections to work; you must be eligible to vote in Minnesota, and people who speak Hmong, Somali, Spanish, Oromo, Amharic, Lao, or ASL are especially wanted

poll_work.name: Minneapolis Elections & Voter Services: student election judges
poll_work.offers: high school students 16 and older who are U.S. citizens living in Hennepin or a nearby metro county can work a Minneapolis polling place; $17.15 an hour (or volunteer), a three-hour training, and an 8- or 15-hour shift; a parent, and during the school year a principal, must give permission

poll_work.name: Ramsey County Elections: election judges
poll_work.offers: sign-ups for adult and student (16 and 17) election judges at polling places and early voting in Ramsey County, which runs Saint Paul's elections; paid by default, from $16 an hour for precinct and student judges to $22 for early-voting judges, after a two-hour training, or you can volunteer

poll_work.name: Duluth City Clerk: be an election judge
poll_work.offers: the application to work one of the city's 34 precincts, from 6 a.m. to about 9 p.m.; the page lists pay of $13 an hour ($15 for head judges), or you can volunteer, and 16- and 17-year-olds can serve as trainees

poll_work.name: St. Louis County Elections: election judge interest form
poll_work.offers: a form to say you'd like to work as an election judge, absentee ballot board judge, early-voting judge, or student trainee (16 or 17); the county passes it to the cities or townships you pick, and pay varies by city and township

poll_work.name: New Jersey Division of Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: the statewide application, which goes to your county board of elections; paid $21.43 an hour on early voting days and $300 for Election Day; you must live in New Jersey, be a U.S. citizen registered to vote in your county, and be 16 or older (under-18s work shorter shifts and needn't be registered), and you can't be a candidate in that election

poll_work.name: Essex County Board of Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: applications to download and email to the board (essexelections@clerk.essexcountynj.org), with a separate student application; $21.44 an hour on early voting days and $300 for Election Day; adults must be registered voters, 18 or older, take a required training class, and work the full day, 5:15 a.m. to 8:30 p.m.; questions go to 862-234-4321

poll_work.name: Union County Board of Elections: poll workers
poll_work.offers: separate online applications for Election Day and early voting; $300 for Election Day, plus $12.50 each for picking up and returning your district's supplies, about 5:15 a.m. to 8:15 p.m.; you must be a Union County voter 18 or older, or 16 or 17 for up to 8 hours; first-timers take a two-hour training in person, required every two years, and skipping it cuts your pay to minimum wage

poll_work.name: Camden County Board of Elections: poll workers
poll_work.offers: the online application; $300 for Election Day, 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., after a required training; you must be 16 or older and registered to vote in Camden County, and bilingual workers are especially needed in Camden City, Pennsauken, and Woodlynne; questions go to (856) 401-8683

poll_work.name: Fulton County Registration and Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: a link to apply, through a staffing company's job portal, for early voting poll worker, polling-place technician, warehouse, and temporary office jobs; you must be a U.S. citizen, 16 or older, and live in Fulton or have a signed waiver from an adjoining county; Election Day runs 5 a.m. to about 11 p.m. at more than 175 polling places, with required in-person training that's paid only if you work Election Day; the page says people who worked the last election get priority, and it doesn't list pay (questions: 404-612-7020)

poll_work.name: DeKalb County Voter Registration and Elections: poll officials
poll_work.offers: the online application for poll manager, assistant manager, and clerk jobs; you must be a U.S. citizen, 16 or older, and live or work in DeKalb (the county isn't taking waivers from other counties now), and you can't hold public office or be a candidate, or a candidate's relative, at your poll; you train, help set up before Election Day, and work from 5:30 a.m. until the polls close; the page says the work is paid but doesn't say how much

poll_work.name: Cobb County Elections: Election Day poll worker jobs
poll_work.offers: the online application, kept on file for future elections; paid $180 an election for clerks, $200 for backup managers, $225 for assistant managers, and $275 for managers (who must have worked an election first), plus $30 for setup and $20 to $95 for the required training before each election; Election Day runs 6 a.m. to about 9 p.m.; you must be 16 or older, a U.S. citizen, and live in or work for Cobb (or a neighboring county, with a waiver), with no felony conviction in 10 years, and you're called when the county needs workers (770-528-2581)

poll_work.name: Lawrenceville City Clerk: poll workers
poll_work.offers: how to work the polls in city elections, which the City Clerk runs: call 678-407-6391 or email the clerk; you must be a U.S. citizen living in the county, 16 or older, able to read, write, and speak English, and free of felony convictions for 10 years, and you must attend training; the page says poll workers are paid but not how much; the next city general election is Nov. 2, 2027

poll_work.name: Chatham County Board of Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: how to apply, online or in person at 1117 Eisenhower Drive, Suite F, Savannah (weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a photo ID), with a background check; new workers start as poll clerks, and pay runs $75 to $320 an election depending on the job, plus training pay if you finish all training and work the whole day; Election Day starts by 6 a.m. and you can't leave the polls; you must live in Chatham, be 16 or older, and not be related to a candidate (912-201-4375)

poll_work.name: Muscogee County Elections and Registration: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: the elections office's home page, which says you must be 16 or older to work the polls and asks you to email muscogeepollworkers@columbusga.org to learn more; it doesn't list pay, training, or hours (questions: 706-653-4392)

poll_work.name: Athens-Clarke County Elections: poll worker information
poll_work.offers: what poll clerks, assistant coordinators, and coordinators do and how to apply when jobs are posted (applications for the Nov. 3, 2026 election were open Aug. 1 to 23); pay is about $15 to $18 an hour, only if you work an election, after required training; Election Day starts by 6 a.m., lunch is provided, and new workers may be on standby; you must be a U.S. citizen living in Athens-Clarke, 16 or older, and high school students can work with their principal's OK (706-613-3150)

poll_work.name: Gwinnett County Elections: be a poll official
poll_work.offers: a link to apply, hiring events, and what Election Day is like: about 3,000 poll officials, at their home precinct when possible, from 5:30 a.m. until closing work is done (plan on 14 hours or more), after an online course and, for some jobs, two to four hours of in-person training; the county's elections FAQ lists pay with training of $160 for non-issuing clerks, $325 for issuing clerks, $390 for assistant managers, and $490 for managers, paid about four weeks after the election; new hires must show proof of U.S. citizenship
